review_state: RTX8000 matched direct 225K prompt plus 128-token compute took 18.4% less time than stock Bonsai; the grouped Q8 attention engine then cut measured 225K depth-only decode time by 28.3%. RTX3090 clean custom runtime took 13.1% less time for a matched 225K prompt plus 128 tokens and 22.4% less timed decode time at 225K depth. Production endpoints remain stock; endpoint TTFT, generated text comparison, and stability evidence remain outstanding.

requirements.finding: Prism adfffbe loader, graph, KV and sampling reused through existing endpoint ABI; no new front end.

requirements.requirement: Packed resident weights; no model-sized expansion
requirements.finding: Packed weights remain in VRAM; bounded unpacked int8 tiles live only in shared memory. Global scratch holds Q8 activations, not expanded model weights. GPU memory proof pending.

requirements.requirement: Original arithmetic, scales and Hadamard transforms
requirements.finding: Owner-approved PQ2/Q8 integer path, existing Prism quantizer, half weight scales and per32 float activation scales; dispatch remains after graph Hadamard handling. Floating accumulation order still requires numeric proof.

Pinned CUTLASS4.8.0 SM75 integer TensorOp. The tuned 128x128x128 eight-warp candidate preserves PQ2/Q8 arithmetic and passed direct correctness on two representative products plus an odd tail. Same-binary RTX8000 operator comparisons beat Bonsai by 12.0% and 11.9%; full-model prefill remains unmeasured.

Three original tile/pipeline combinations and one tuned 128x128x128 single-stage candidate remain registered. Direct RTX8000 tests show the tuned candidate more than 10% faster than Bonsai on two shapes. Hadamard transforms remain upstream; transform fusion and full-model tuning are unmeasured. RTX3090 follows the owner sequence.

Four-row Q8/DP4A decode passed 26/26 direct CPU-reference cases and beat stock Bonsai by more than 5% at batches 1/2/4/8 on three representative RTX8000 matrix shapes. Matched full-model 225K depth decode improved 28.3% on RTX8000 and 22.4% on RTX3090 with the combined grouped-attention engine; the matrix kernel's separate share of those gains is unmeasured.
Four CUTLASS candidates compete with native decode when compatible; unsupported fusion contracts retain reference.
Compatible candidates use architecture, format, matrix shape, actual microbatch workload classification and fusion signature.

Actual n_seqs_unq and n_tokens propagated from llama process_ubatch through central ggml-base thread-local storage; phase is token multiplicity or encoder graph type, not endpoint request intent. Matrix N remains independent. Unknown metadata uses reference. ProfileV2 and receipt schema2 verify distinct workload identities.

requirements.requirement: Startup warmup and persisted median calibration
requirements.finding: Metadata-derived representative shapes; explicit startup process invokes real backend graphs; two warmups and five event samples per route. Direct graph-case execution passed; full-model startup profile behavior remains unverified.

requirements.requirement: Fastest correct candidate and unseen-shape reference
requirements.finding: Full-output finite/NMSE comparison and strict median improvement required; unprofiled/unsafe shapes keep Prism. Forced direct RTX8000 operator tests show faster custom decode and prefill candidates, but a calibrated profile selecting them in full-model inference remains unverified.
Fingerprint includes GPU UUID/arch, driver/runtime, nvcc/host compiler and engine/Prism/CUTLASS revisions.

Uncaptured per-kernel and captured whole-graph completion samples invalidate persisted profiles. Device epoch and workload identity force cached graph recapture. Graph-cohort drift does not establish an individual kernel cause. Explicit startup calibration retests. Host controls pass; GPU replay proof pending.

SM75 backend initialization reserves128MiB for stream0 only when calibration or a measured faster CUTLASS route warrants it. Additional eligible mapped streams reserve before capture, at most8slabs/1GiB percontext. Stable addresses survive graphs; synchronized backend teardown frees them. Candidate launches allocate nothing. GPU load-memory proof pending.

Operator/calibration timing, sampled actual graph completion, route and actual workload, used/reserved scratch, shared-per-block storage and endpoint timing are instrumented. Direct graph-case timings and matched 225K full-model throughput were collected on RTX8000 and RTX3090. Logical operand byte footprints are estimates; physical DRAM transactions remain unmeasured.

requirements.requirement: KV capacity, prefix reuse and context pressure
requirements.finding: Existing endpoint/Prism KV implementation retained; long-context and prefix regression tests not run for new engine.

CUDA candidates now under engine/backends/cuda/{prefill_cutlass,decode_ternary}; shared dispatch, telemetry and tests under engine/. Core/formats/KV supplied by pinned Prism, without empty replacement modules. Existing benchmark tooling remains at repository root.

requirements.requirement: Correctness/logits, stability and speed acceptance gates
requirements.finding: Direct CPU-reference correctness passed for optimized decode, prefill and attention cases, including grouped Q8 attention at 225K on clean SM75 and SM86 libraries. Matched 225K prompt-plus-generation compute took 18.4% less time on RTX8000 and 13.1% less on RTX3090; depth-only decode took 28.3% and 22.4% less, respectively, with the grouped engine. The benchmarks do not compare generated text or measure endpoint TTFT. Long-run stability, batching/prefix behavior and isolated weight VRAM remain unverified.

RTX8000 direct long-context compute exceeds the 10% goal and grouped decode is 28.3% faster at 225K. RTX3090 matched direct 225K prompt-plus-generation compute is 13.1% faster and depth decode is 22.4% faster. The stock 3090 endpoint was temporarily stopped for the direct pair and restored unchanged. P40 follows the 3090 goal, then R9700; Ryzen is excluded.
No SpecKit work until viable/functioning; subtree gate waived only.
